scope: Bavarian G9 Grade 11 Einführungsklasse where biology is offered; the ISB implementation guidance applies from 2023/24.
numbering: Within each area, the second component numbers competency bullets in the official source order. Descriptions are English paraphrases.

coverage.competence: Formulate testable biological questions and plan qualitative and quantitative investigations from a hypothesis.
coverage.evidence: Plan a controlled yeast comparison; design a pH series or a one-factor dummy trial.

coverage.competence: Carry out and independently document, display and evaluate investigations.
coverage.evidence: Simulate a measurement series; move from observations to a table and graph; practise the sequence of a microscope investigation. The real experiment and use of lab equipment require classwork.

coverage.competence: Judge data validity and identify trends, structures and relationships.
coverage.evidence: Compare repeats, means and ranges; isolate treatment effects and assess confounding factors.

coverage.competence: Identify the limits and scope of knowledge produced by an investigation.
coverage.evidence: Constrain the temperature optimum to the measured range and the behavior claim to the tested learning opportunity.

coverage.competence: Model biological processes, propose alternatives and compare their strengths and limitations.
coverage.evidence: Contrast an activity curve and an active-site model; test denaturation against a leak, and compare predictions from a gas exchange model.

coverage.competence: Distinguish everyday from scientific language and select information sources for a question and audience.
coverage.evidence: Translate a claim into a bounded statement; assess author, method, audience and date before using BIÖG or DGE material.

coverage.competence: Develop options using biological evidence, weigh criteria and revisit a decision.
coverage.evidence: Compare two school options by access, cost and health, and state when to reconsider; discuss barriers to vaccine participation.

coverage.competence: Weigh effects of behavior and measures on personal and public health.
coverage.evidence: Compare transmission-specific measures, indirect protection, and an everyday food choice.

coverage.competence: Use a microscope to examine the structure of plant and animal tissues.
coverage.evidence: Choose an objective and center a simulated specimen; interpret and sketch classroom specimens in supervised lab work.

coverage.competence: Distinguish animal and plant cells in microscopic images and diagrams.
coverage.evidence: Compare schematic fields and labeled organelles; distinguish an epidermal specimen from a green leaf.

coverage.competence: Compare the structure and life functions of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
coverage.evidence: Compare nucleus, DNA, ribosomes and energy metabolism; contrast the forms and locations of the genetic material.

coverage.competence: Use cell structure to justify the classification of organisms.
coverage.evidence: Classify four specimens by combinations of nucleus, wall composition and chloroplasts; identify the limits of the images.

coverage.competence: Describe interactions between humans and organisms on or inside the body and derive health-conscious behavior.
coverage.evidence: Distinguish helpful colonization, infection and parasitism, and match protection to a route.

coverage.competence: Distinguish bacterial from viral infections using examples.
coverage.evidence: Compare binary fission and a phage cycle; explain why a drug targeting bacterial walls does not affect influenza.

coverage.competence: Explain the main innate and specific defenses.
coverage.evidence: Classify barriers, inflammatory responses, specific antibody responses and immune memory.

coverage.competence: Explain immunization and the role of preventive vaccination.
coverage.evidence: Compare first response, memory response and passive antibodies on a common scale; analyze when indirect protection is possible.

coverage.competence: Describe the human body as an open system requiring materials and energy carriers.
coverage.evidence: Track matter across the body boundary, internal transformations, energy transfer and involved systems.

coverage.competence: Classify food macronutrients from their molecular structures.
coverage.evidence: Classify sugars by number of units, fats by glycerol and fatty acids, and proteins by amino acids.

coverage.competence: Use macro- and micronutrient functions and food composition to plan a balanced diet for a context.
coverage.evidence: Justify suitable school-day foods and account for availability, tolerability and relevant nutrients.

coverage.competence: Explain enzymes at the substance and particle levels, using energy and lock-and-key models.
coverage.evidence: Explain starch breakdown and the activation barrier; vary temperature, pH and substrate in a model.

coverage.competence: Explain food transport and stepwise breakdown into absorbable particles.
coverage.evidence: Order digestive stations and compare carbohydrates, proteins and fats; distinguish emulsification from chemical breakdown.

coverage.competence: Relate the structure of the small intestine to absorption.
coverage.evidence: Relate folds, villi and microvilli to surface area; compare transport mechanisms and routes into blood and lymph.

coverage.competence: Explain gas exchange by diffusion using the structure–function relationship.
coverage.evidence: Vary surface area, distance and gradient; follow the opposing directions of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

coverage.competence: Explain circulation as a transport system linking the environment with body cells.
coverage.evidence: Follow oxygen through both circuits and relate transport to hemoglobin, exchange and return flow.

coverage.competence: Describe aerobic glucose breakdown as an exothermic redox reaction and explain the ATP–ADP cycle.
coverage.evidence: Classify inputs, products, energy transfer and ATP use; compare ATP renewal and consumption.

coverage.competence: Compare glucose breakdown in respiration with glucose production in photosynthesis.
coverage.evidence: Compare net equations and energy conversion; interpret net gas exchange in light and dark without assuming respiration stops.

coverage.competence: Use structural diversity to explain different functions of proteins.
coverage.evidence: Connect sequence and folding to fibers, oxygen binding and catalysis.

coverage.competence: Explain how the structure of DNA enables it to store information.
coverage.evidence: Read paired strands in both directions; distinguish the base sequence from the sugar-phosphate backbone.

coverage.competence: Explain the basic steps of protein synthesis and how proteins contribute to traits.
coverage.evidence: Order transcription, translation, folding and enzyme action; discuss why the same sequence need not produce the same observed trait.

coverage.competence: Compare how prokaryotes and eukaryotes organize genetic material.
coverage.evidence: Compare bacterial chromosomes and plasmids with nuclear chromosomes; interpret what a karyogram can show.

coverage.competence: Explain why DNA is replicated and demonstrate its basic mechanism with a model.
coverage.evidence: Pair model strands and explain one old and one new strand per double helix; distinguish DNA and chromosome counts.

coverage.competence: Describe the cell cycle and its role in growth, regeneration and asexual reproduction.
coverage.evidence: Order interphase, copying, nuclear division and cytokinesis; count chromosomes and chromatids before and after.

coverage.competence: Explain meiotic division and its role in sexual reproduction and variation.
coverage.evidence: Separate homologues and chromatids in two divisions; change pair orientation and restore the diploid set at fertilization.

coverage.competence: Explain the neuron and information transfer from a sense organ to an effector.
coverage.evidence: Trace afferent and efferent pathways; compare successful chemical transmission and receptor blockade.

coverage.competence: Compare behaviors in dummy experiments as effects of both external cues and internal factors.
coverage.evidence: Change one condition at a time and compare model observations; separate the observable behavior from the inferred state.

coverage.competence: Use observations to judge genetic and acquired components of behavior.
coverage.evidence: Separate a shared call pattern from a learned transition, weigh alternative explanations and discuss the limits of historical isolation experiments.
